title: Flames sign defenseman Šimon Nemec to 5-year, $7.25 million AAV contract
content:
The Calgary Flames have signed defenseman Šimon Nemec to a five-year, $36.25 million contract carrying a $7.25 million annual average value, the team announced Monday.

The 22-year-old was acquired in a trade with the New Jersey Devils on June 23 and was a restricted free agent. Nemec scored 11 goals and 26 points in 68 games with the Devils last season.

Nemec was chosen No. 2 by the Devils during the 2022 NHL Draft and spent parts of three seasons with the franchise before the deal. The defenseman scored 16 goals and 49 points in 155 career games with the Devils. Nemec has also represented Slovakia at the international level, winning an Olympic bronze medal with Slovakia in 2022. Forward Maxim Tsyplakov was also acquired by the Flames in their trade with the Devils.

In Calgary, Nemec will be counted on for his offense as the franchise continues its rebuild. Nemec’s 11 goals last season would have led all Flames blueliners — ahead of Rasmus Andersson, who scored 10 in 48 games before being traded to the Vegas Golden Knights. Nemec will also be leaned on for his power-play abilities while guiding along top prospect Zayne Parekh on the team’s back end.

According to PuckPedia, the Flames now have over $14 million in cap space this offseason. The Flames have been busy, trading winger Blake Coleman and defenseman Olli Määttä to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for Jake Middleton and draft picks.

Nemec will enter the upcoming season as the team’s most experienced offensive defenseman for a franchise still accumulating young talent wherever possible. General manager Craig Conroy has long coveted players between 18 and 23 years old, and Nemec fits the bill as a talented, right-shot defenseman who was clamoring for more ice time and responsibility in New Jersey.

Between Nemec and Parekh, the Flames now have two talented puck-moving defenders they can cultivate and lean on for offense. But Nemec will likely start as the team’s top power-play quarterback. Nemec could easily start the season as a top-pairing option either alongside Kevin Bahl (who spent part of last season with Zach Whitecloud) or the newly-acquired Middleton in a top-four role.

According to AFP Analytics’ projections, Nemec was slated to sign a long-term contract of seven years with a $8,060,650 cap hit. Nemec’s real-life deal is shorter while carrying a lesser cap hit. His $7.25 million AAV will fit just fine under Calgary’s cap structure, especially since they’re not expected to be big spenders as a rebuilding team. Though the Flames will certainly listen if there’s an opportunity to strike a deal to net another young talent like they did with Nemec.
